editorial:
You follow one strange day with a man who keeps changing into different people from the back of a limo. He becomes a beggar, a monster, a father, and more, with each stop feeling like a new short story. The movie is weird, dreamlike, and sometimes funny, but it also has quiet, sad moments. You never know what is coming next, and that surprise keeps you watching even when the plot feels loose.

The acting is the big draw, especially the lead, who throws himself into every role with full energy. The pacing jumps around, so some scenes fly by while others slow down and breathe. Pros: bold ideas, strong performances, and images you will remember. Cons: it can be confusing, and it is not for viewers who want a normal story. If you like strange, artful movies, give it a try. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or buy the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Oscar returns to the limo garage, where the cars talk to each other about being tired and old. Then he goes home to a family of chimpanzees, hinting that his own life may also be another performance. The twist is that every identity, even the quiet home life, feels staged, so you are left wondering what is real.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves strange, dreamlike movies.
